verifyNote: Standard codes are references. Check the marking on the product and the current edition. Indian codes marked verify should be confirmed before audit use.
selection_rules: PPE is the last line of defence. Use elimination, substitution and engineering controls first
PPE must fit the person and be compatible with other PPE (for example glasses with respirator)
Train workers to put on, use, inspect and store PPE
Keep a record of issue, inspection and replacement
Choose certified PPE with the correct standard marking for your country
Never use damaged PPE. Tag it out and replace it

helmet.name: Safety helmet

standards.usa: ANSI/ISEA Z89.1 (Type I top impact, Type II top and lateral; Class E for electrical)

helmet.protects_against: Falling objects, bumps, electrical contact (Class E)
choose: Choose the type for the hazard: lateral impact, electrical, high heat
Use a chin strap when working at height or in wind
Do not paint, drill or put stickers over the shell

safety_glasses.name: Safety glasses
safety_glasses.protects_against: Flying particles, dust, UV, splashes (with side shields)
choose: Look for the marking on the frame and lens (for example Z87+ or EN 166 F for impact)
Wear over prescription glasses only if designed for it or use prescription safety glasses
Choose tinted lenses for outdoor sun

goggles.name: Splash goggles

standards.eu: EN 166 (field of use 3 liquid splash, 4 dust, 5 gas)
standards.usa: ANSI/ISEA Z87.1 (D3 splash, D4 dust, D5 fine dust)

choose: Indirect vent goggles for splash
Sealed goggles for fine dust and gas
Check compatibility with your respirator

face_shield.name: Face shield

standards.eu: EN 166 (3 splash, 8 electric arc, 9 molten metal)

face_shield.protects_against: Splash, sparks, grinding fragments, arc flash (arc-rated type)
choose: Always wear safety glasses under a face shield
For arc flash use an arc-rated shield with a suitable rating

welding_helmet.name: Welding helmet
choose: Choose the shade for the process and amperage (commonly shade 10 to 13)
Use auto-darkening with a manual backup
Wear safety glasses under the helmet

earplugs.name: Ear plugs
choose: Choose by the noise level and the rating (SNR or NRR) so you are not over-protected
Train workers to insert plugs deeply and correctly
Use corded plugs for easy removal

earmuffs.name: Ear muffs
choose: Good for on and off use
Check that they seal over hair, hard hats and glasses arms
Combine with plugs for very high noise

respirator_particle.name: Respirator for dust and fume

standards.eu: EN 149 filtering facepiece FFP1, FFP2, FFP3
standards.canada: CSA Z94.4 (selection, use and care); NIOSH-approved devices accepted

choose: Choose the class for the hazard (FFP3 or P100 for toxic dust and welding fume)
Fit test before first use and annually. No beard under the seal
Replace when breathing becomes hard or the mask is damaged or wet

respirator_gas.name: Respirator for gas and vapour

standards.eu: EN 140 half mask or EN 136 full face with EN 14387 gas and combined filters
standards.usa: NIOSH-approved half or full facepiece with organic vapour or combination cartridges

respirator_gas.protects_against: Solvent vapour, acid gas, ammonia (type K)
choose: Match the filter type and colour to the gas using the SDS
Change cartridges on a schedule or when you smell or taste the contaminant
Not for oxygen-poor air

air_fed.name: Air-fed or breathing apparatus
air_fed.protects_against: Oxygen-poor air, unknown atmospheres, abrasive blasting, high toxic concentrations
choose: Only trained and medically fit users
Check breathing air quality and pressure every shift
Always keep a trained standby for entry work

escape_set.name: Escape breathing set
escape_set.protects_against: Sudden release of H2S or toxic gas
choose: Carry within reach at all times in gas areas
Train every user to don it within seconds
Check pressure and seals as the manufacturer says

gloves_mech.name: Mechanical protection gloves

standards.eu: EN 388 (abrasion, cut, tear, puncture; EN ISO 13997 cut level A to F)

choose: Match cut level to the task, not the highest level for everything
Avoid loose gloves near rotating machinery
Choose grip type for wet or oily work

gloves_chem.name: Chemical-resistant gloves

standards.eu: EN ISO 374-1 (types A, B, C) and EN ISO 374-5
standards.usa: ANSI/ISEA 105 chemical ratings; ASTM F739 permeation

choose: Choose the glove material from the SDS and the manufacturer chemical chart
Check breakthrough time against the task length
Do not reuse after heavy contact

gloves_heat.name: Welding and heat gloves
choose: Choose by contact heat level
Dry gloves only. Wet gloves conduct heat
Do not use for live electrical work

gloves_insulating.name: Insulating gloves (electrical)

standards.usa: ASTM D120 (Class 00 to 4), worn with leather protectors; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.137

choose: Choose the class for the voltage
Air test before every use and keep electrical test dates current (about every 6 months in service in the US)
Always wear leather protectors over them

gloves_cold.name: Cold-protection gloves
choose: Choose insulation for the temperature and the dexterity needed
Keep spare dry gloves

boots.name: Safety footwear

standards.eu: EN ISO 20345 (SB basic, S1, S1P, S3; SRC slip resistance)
standards.usa: ASTM F2413 (I/75 C/75 plus EH, PR, Mt)
standards.canada: CSA Z195 (green triangle toe, green rectangle sole puncture)

boots.protects_against: Crush, puncture, slips, electrical hazard (EH), metatarsal (Mt)
choose: Choose toecap, midsole puncture plate and slip rating for the work
Wellington style for wet and chemical areas
Replace when the sole is worn smooth or the toecap is exposed

harness.name: Full body harness and lanyard

standards.eu: EN 361 harness, EN 355 energy absorber, EN 795 anchor devices, EN 363 systems

choose: Choose the harness type for the task (rescue loops, positioning belt, work at height)
Fit adjustment before each use and match to the user's size
Plan rescue before work starts

hivis.name: High-visibility clothing

standards.usa: ANSI/ISEA 107 (Type O, R, P; Class 1 to 3)

hivis.protects_against: Being struck by vehicles and plant
choose: Class 2 or 3 near traffic
Replace when faded, dirty or tape peels
Lighter fabrics help in the heat

fr_arc.name: Arc-rated clothing

standards.usa: NFPA 70E, ASTM F1506, arc rating in cal/cm2

choose: Choose the arc rating from the arc flash study
Wear natural or arc-rated underlayers only (no melting synthetics)
Keep clean and undamaged

fr_coverall.name: Flame-resistant coverall

standards.canada: CSA Z96 or CSA Z462 as relevant

choose: Required in many oil and gas and process areas
Never wear synthetic underwear that melts
Follow wash instructions so protection is not lost

welding_clothing.name: Welding clothing and apron
choose: Class 2 for heavier welding and overhead work
Leather apron and sleeves for heavy spatter
Buttoned collars and no turn-ups where sparks can collect

chem_suit.name: Chemical protective suit

standards.eu: EN 943 (gas tight), EN 14605 (liquid tight types 3 and 4), EN 13034 (type 6), EN 13982 (type 5 particles)

choose: Match suit type to the physical state: gas, liquid, particle
Limit wear time because suits trap heat
Train on putting on and taking off to avoid contamination

blast_suit.name: Abrasive blasting suit
choose: Worn with an air-fed blasting helmet
Heavy leather or reinforced fabric

cold_clothing.name: Cold protective clothing

standards.usa: ASTM F1060 and cold work standards

choose: Use layers: base, insulation, shell
Keep dry and have a spare set
Cover head, hands, face and feet

lifejacket.name: Lifejacket or buoyancy aid

standards.usa: USCG approved; SOLAS and LSA Code for ships

choose: Choose automatic inflatable or foam for the job
Inspect gas cylinders and bladders on a schedule
Wear it fastened and with a crotch strap where fitted

sun_protection.name: Sun protection
choose: Broad-brim hat or helmet neck cover
UV 400 tinted safety glasses
Sunscreen on exposed skin

hygiene_wear.name: Food hygiene wear

standards.india: Site food safety standard and FSSAI where relevant

choose: Hairnet, beard cover, clean outer clothing
No jewellery
Colour code by zone if the site uses it

tasks.label: General site entry
tasks.note: Minimum for most sites. Add more for the task.

tasks.label: Welding and hot work
tasks.note: Add extraction and a fire watch. Respirator for stainless and galvanised steel fume.

tasks.label: Work at height
tasks.note: Helmet with chin strap. Rescue plan before work.

tasks.label: Electrical work
tasks.note: Use Class E helmet and EH boots. Arc rating from the arc flash study.

tasks.label: Confined space entry
tasks.note: Breathing apparatus where the air is not proven safe. Gas detector and rescue plan are essential.

tasks.label: High noise area
tasks.note: Use both for very high noise. Check fit.

tasks.label: Abrasive blasting
tasks.note: Air-fed helmet only. Check breathing air quality.

tasks.label: Cold room and cold store
tasks.note: Limit time and use rewarming breaks.

tasks.label: Outdoor heat
tasks.note: See the heat stress adjustments below.

tasks.label: Marine deck work
tasks.note: Chin strap. Lifejacket where there is an overboard risk.

tasks.label: Oil and gas process area
tasks.note: Plus a personal gas detector. Flame-resistant clothing with no melting underwear.

tasks.label: Food processing and sanitation
tasks.note: Non-slip boots with SRC rating. Cut gloves where blades are used.

inspection.name: Full body harness and lanyard
before_use: Read the label: it must be legible and show the date
Check all webbing along its full length by running it through your hands
Check stitching, buckles, D-rings and attachment points
Check the energy absorber pack is intact and not deployed
Check connectors and gates close and lock fully
reject_if: Cuts, fraying, burns, melting, hard or stiff areas
Chemical damage, paint, heavy dirt or UV fading
Cracked, bent, corroded or sharp-edged metal parts
Energy absorber deployed or label missing
care: Store dry, away from sunlight, chemicals and sharp objects
Competent person inspection at set intervals and record it
inspection.life: Follow the manufacturer's instructions. Many sites inspect formally every 3 to 12 months.

inspection.name: Safety helmet
before_use: Check the shell for cracks, dents, chalking or fading
Check the suspension and headband are intact and adjust properly
Check the chin strap and buckle work
Check the date mark inside the shell
reject_if: Cracks or deep scratches in the shell
Hit by a heavy impact, even if no damage is visible
Drilled, painted with solvent or glued stickers hiding damage
care: Clean with mild soap and water
Do not store in a hot car
Do not put hard objects on top
inspection.life: Follow the manufacturer. Many sites replace polyethylene helmets about every 3 to 5 years, or after impact.

inspection.name: Respirator
before_use: Check the facepiece for cracks, splits or warping
Check valves, seals and straps are clean and flexible
Check the filter is the right type, in date and not damaged or wet
Do a seal check every time you put it on
Confirm you have passed a fit test for this model
reject_if: Filter past expiry, damaged, wet or clogged
Breathing becomes hard or you taste or smell the contaminant
care: Store in a clean sealed bag away from dust and chemicals
Disposable masks are single shift use or per the site rule
inspection.life: Cartridge and filter change schedule from the SDS and the site respiratory programme.

inspection.name: Gloves
before_use: Check for holes, cuts, thin patches and stiff areas
Check inside for contamination
Insulating gloves: air test and check the electrical test date
reject_if: Holes, cuts, tears or worn through
Swollen, sticky, hard or discoloured from chemicals
Insulating gloves out of test date or with any damage
care: Wash and dry as the maker advises
Store flat, away from heat and sunlight
Replace by task, not by a calendar
inspection.life: Replace when damaged. Insulating gloves must stay within their electrical test interval.

inspection.name: Safety glasses and goggles
before_use: Check lenses for scratches, cracks and pitting
Check frame and side shields are secure
Check the markings are visible and correct for the hazard
Check the strap is elastic and the vents are clear
care: Clean with lens cleaner and a soft cloth

inspection.name: Ear plugs and ear muffs
before_use: Muffs: check cushions for cracks and hardness and that the headband still clamps well
Plugs: check they are clean, soft and not deformed
Check the correct protection rating for the noise
reject_if: Muffs that do not seal over glasses or a helmet
inspection.life: Replace cushions regularly and plugs when dirty.

inspection.name: Safety boots
before_use: Check the sole tread and the heel
Check the toecap: no exposed or crushed steel or composite
Check the upper for cuts and split seams
Check for midsole puncture or separation
care: Clean and keep laces in good condition
inspection.life: Replace when worn or after a heavy impact on the toecap.

inspection.name: High-visibility clothing
before_use: Check colour is bright and not faded
Check reflective tape is not peeling or cracked
Check the garment is clean and fits properly
reject_if: Faded or stained so it no longer stands out
care: Wash by the label and do not use fabric softener
inspection.life: Replace when colour or tape no longer meets the standard.

heat_stress.principle: Heat stress PPE adjustments never remove protection from the real hazard. Change the work method, schedule or controls before reducing PPE.

adjustments.issue: Heavy flame-resistant or chemical clothing traps heat
adjustments.adjust: Use lighter breathable FR fabrics where the standard allows, shorten wear time and add work-rest cycles
Strictly limit time, monitor heart rate or core temperature and add cooling and rest breaks
Consider powered air or air-fed hoods with cooled air for long tasks
Use light colours, ventilated helmets, neck shades and sweat bands
Choose breathable materials and spare dry socks and gloves
Phase-change vests work in dry heat. Evaporative vests do much less in very humid heat
UV 400 safety glasses, sunscreen and neck cover
Use lighter-weight mesh style hi-vis that still meets the class

rules: Provide cool drinking water and electrolytes, and rest in shade
Use a buddy system and know the signs: dizziness, confusion, hot dry skin, collapse
Do not remove PPE that protects from a real hazard to cool down: stop the job and use a cool area
Follow national midday work bans where they apply
